raw_text: In LMMM, evaporative cooling system of Walking beam furnace is provided with 2 nos of steam turbines to cater to the feed water recirculation in ECS circuits. The requirement of steam turbine is most vital especially in case of any power failure and also during initial starting of ECS after any furnace shutdown. The turbines have been running since inception and due to the prolonged use, the wear out of the internals including the rotor shafts has increased.
normalized_text: IN LMMM EVAPORATIVE COOLING SYSTEM OF WALKING BEAM FURNACE IS PROVIDED WITH 2 NOS OF STEAM TURBINES TO CATER TO THE FEED WATER RECIRCULATION IN ECS CIRCUITS THE REQUIREMENT OF STEAM TURBINE IS MOST VITAL ESPECIALLY IN CASE OF ANY POWER FAILURE AND ALSO DURING INITIAL STARTING OF ECS AFTER ANY FURNACE SHUTDOWN THE TURBINES HAVE BEEN RUNNING SINCE INCEPTION AND DUE TO THE PROLONGED USE THE WEAR OUT OF THE INTERNALS INCLUDING THE ROTOR SHAFTS HAS INCREASED

raw_text: The proposal to refurbish the worn out shaft with the help of external agencies didn’t materialise as it was too expensive. Instead of going for procurement of a new rotor due to the high cost involved, dept team has revisioned the rotor shaft in-house using powder metallurgy .
normalized_text: THE PROPOSAL TO REFURBISH THE WORN OUT SHAFT WITH THE HELP OF EXTERNAL AGENCIES DIDN T MATERIALISE AS IT WAS TOO EXPENSIVE INSTEAD OF GOING FOR PROCUREMENT OF A NEW ROTOR DUE TO THE HIGH COST INVOLVED DEPT TEAM HAS REVISIONED THE ROTOR SHAFT IN HOUSE USING POWDER METALLURGY

raw_text: The worn out area of the rotor shaft especially the bearing seating area was initially built up by fusewelding using Colmonoy 27 and 63F alloy powder which was found compatible with the shaft material. The built up surface was then gradually rounded off by grinding, using a jig and fixture arrangement to get a uniformly well rounded shaft.
normalized_text: THE WORN OUT AREA OF THE ROTOR SHAFT ESPECIALLY THE BEARING SEATING AREA WAS INITIALLY BUILT UP BY FUSEWELDING USING COLMONOY 27 AND 63F ALLOY POWDER WHICH WAS FOUND COMPATIBLE WITH THE SHAFT MATERIAL THE BUILT UP SURFACE WAS THEN GRADUALLY ROUNDED OFF BY GRINDING USING A JIG AND FIXTURE ARRANGEMENT TO GET A UNIFORMLY WELL ROUNDED SHAFT

raw_text: A spare rotor shaft was made ready with minimum cost with available in house resources.
normalized_text: A SPARE ROTOR SHAFT WAS MADE READY WITH MINIMUM COST WITH AVAILABLE IN HOUSE RESOURCES
